passages.title: Sailing Lessons and the Forecast
sentences: The Harbor Sailing School teaches young sailors in small boats called dinghies.
Each lesson lasts two hours and takes place in the calm water inside the harbor wall.
An instructor follows every group in a motor boat.
On Saturday, lessons start at 8 AM, 10 AM, 1 PM and 3 PM.
Before each lesson, the instructors study the hourly forecast.
A dinghy is small and light, so strong wind makes it hard to steer.
The boats stay at the dock if the wind is over 15 miles per hour (mph) at any hour of the lesson.
They also stay at the dock if the chance of a thunderstorm is 30% or more at any hour of the lesson.
For example, a 10 AM lesson uses the 10 AM row and the 11 AM row of the forecast.
If the boats cannot go out, students stay in the classroom on the dock.
They learn to tie knots and read weather maps instead.
Students who miss a lesson on the water may join a make-up lesson on Sunday at 9 AM.
Students should arrive 15 minutes before their lesson to put on a life jacket.
Life jackets are worn at all times, on the dock and in the boats.

passages.title: Kayak Tours and the Tides
sentences: Otter Bay Kayaks runs guided tours of the bay in two-person sea kayaks.
Every paddler must wear a life jacket, and a trained guide leads each group.
Paddlers must be at least 10 years old, and anyone under 16 shares a kayak with an adult.
The Seal Rock Tour visits a group of rocks where harbor seals often rest in the sun.
The seals climb onto the rocks when the tide is low, and the rocks disappear under the water at high tide.
For this reason, the tour leaves 1 hour before low tide and comes back 1 hour after it.
Guides keep the kayaks at least 50 yards from the seals, so that the animals can rest without being disturbed.
The Kelp Forest Tour paddles over an underwater forest of tall seaweed called kelp, where sea otters often float on their backs.
This tour needs deep water, so it leaves at the time of high tide and lasts 90 minutes.
For safety, no tour leaves before 7:00 AM or comes back after 7:00 PM.
Each tour costs $35 for an adult and $25 for anyone 10 to 15 years old.

passages.title: Shelter Volunteer Shifts
sentences: The Harbor Town Animal Shelter needs volunteers to help care for the dogs and cats that are waiting for new homes.
Volunteers walk dogs, play with cats, wash food bowls, fold clean towels and help keep the animal rooms clean and quiet.
Every new volunteer must first attend a one-hour training class.
After the class, volunteers may work at any job they are old enough to do.
Every volunteer receives a green shirt to wear on each shift.
Volunteers aged 12 to 15 must work with a parent or another adult from their family, while volunteers aged 16 and up may work on their own.
Only volunteers aged 14 and up may walk the dogs, because some of the dogs are large and pull hard on the leash.
Each shift has a limited number of places, shown in the Places left column.
Sign up at the front desk at least two days before a shift.
If you cannot come to a shift, please tell the front desk, so that another volunteer can take your place.
Wear closed shoes, and leave your own pets at home.

passages.title: Park Shuttle and Trails
sentences: On summer weekends, Lantern Peaks Nature Park closes its narrow mountain road to private cars.
Visitors leave their cars at the Park Gate and ride a free shuttle bus up into the hills.
Up shuttles start at the Park Gate and climb all the way to the Summit Trailhead.
Down shuttles start at the Summit Trailhead and stop at every stop on the way back down to the gate.
Three trails begin at the shuttle stops.
The Lakeshore Loop starts and ends at Pine Lake and takes about 1 hour to walk.
The Falls Trail starts and ends at the Waterfall Trailhead and takes about 2 hours, because it climbs beside a steep waterfall.
The Summit Trail climbs to the top of the highest peak and returns to the Summit Trailhead, which takes about 3 hours.
Plan to be at your stop at least 5 minutes before your shuttle is due.
The last shuttle of the day leaves the Summit Trailhead at 5:00 PM.
There is no drinking water for sale beyond the Park Gate, so carry at least one full bottle for each person.
Please stay on the marked trails to protect the plants and animals that live in the park.

items.explain: They get to the campsite at 9:05 AM. Route 2 gets to the Ferry dock at 8:25 AM. The 8:35 AM Route 6 bus leaves 10 minutes later and arrives at 9:05 AM.

items.prompt: Ana and Ben get on the 9:30 AM Route 2 bus. Tap the row for the Route 6 bus they can catch at the Ferry dock.
items.hint: Find when their Route 2 bus gets to the Ferry dock. Read the note to see how long the walk takes. Then check each Route 6 time.
items.explain: Tap the 11:35 AM Route 6 row. Their bus gets to the Ferry dock at 9:55 AM. The 10:00 AM bus leaves only 5 minutes later, and the note says they need at least 10 minutes. So they catch the 11:35 AM bus.

items.prompt: It is 12:30 PM. Leo wants a veggie burger with fries and a lemonade. He also wants to add avocado. How much will he pay?
items.hint: A main dish with a side and a drink is a combo. Check the note for combo times. Then find the combo price and add the extra.
items.explain: Leo pays $10. At 12:30 PM combos are served, and the veggie burger combo is $9. Adding avocado is $1 more, so $9 + $1 = $10.

items.prompt: Maya gets to the café at 4 PM. She wants fish tacos, a fruit cup and a milk. She has $10. What should she do?
options: Order the fish tacos combo for $10.
Order all three on their own. She has enough money.
Order the fish tacos and the fruit cup on their own for $9.50.
Order the veggie burger combo for $9 instead.
items.hint: Read the note to check if combos are served at 4 PM. Then add up the prices on their own and compare with $10.
items.explain: She should order the fish tacos and the fruit cup for $9.50. The note says combos end at 3 PM. All three on their own cost $7 + $2.50 + $2 = $11.50, which is more than $10.

items.prompt: Wednesday, March 4 is an early release day. Priya's mom plans to pick her up after robotics club at 4:45 PM, like on other Wednesdays. What should Priya tell her?
options: Pick me up at 4:45 PM, after robotics club.
Pick me up at 12:45 PM. Robotics club does not meet today.
Pick me up at 2:35 PM, when school ends.
Pick me up at 1:25 PM, after History.
items.hint: Read the note under the table first. Then find when school ends on an early release day.
items.explain: She should say 12:45 PM. The note says robotics club does not meet on early release days, and the School ends row says 12:45 PM in the Early release day column.

items.prompt: Ms. Ortiz teaches Science. On an early release day, how much shorter is her class than on a regular day?
items.hint: Work out how many minutes Science lasts in each column. Then take the smaller number away from the bigger one.
items.explain: It is 20 minutes shorter. In the Science row, the regular class runs 9:50 to 10:45 AM, which is 55 minutes. The early release class runs 9:25 to 10:00 AM, which is 35 minutes. 55 - 35 = 20.

items.prompt: It is a Tuesday. Sam and Grandma Rose take ferry B to Gull Island. They want at least 2 hours at the tide pools. What time does the earliest ferry they can take home leave Gull Island?
items.hint: Add 40 minutes to find when ferry B gets to Gull Island. Add 2 more hours. Then look down the Leaves Gull Island column for the next time, and check the Runs on column.
items.explain: The earliest ferry home leaves Gull Island at 2:00 PM. Ferry B leaves at 10:30 AM and the trip takes 40 minutes, so it arrives at 11:10 AM. Two hours later is 1:10 PM. The next time in the Leaves Gull Island column is 2:00 PM, and ferry C runs on weekdays.

items.prompt: It is a Saturday. Leo and Maya are on Gull Island. They miss the 4:15 PM ferry home. What can they do?
options: Take the 6:00 PM ferry from Gull Island.
Take the 7:00 PM ferry from Gull Island.
Take the 9:00 AM ferry tomorrow. No more ferries leave today.
Take the 6:40 PM ferry from Gull Island.
items.hint: Look down the Leaves Gull Island column for a time after 4:15 PM. Then check the Runs on column for that ferry.
items.explain: They can take the 7:00 PM ferry from Gull Island. It is ferry E, and the Runs on column says Saturday and Sunday only, so it runs today. 6:00 PM is when ferry E leaves Harbor Town.

items.prompt: Maya gets to the front desk at 1:50 PM. She wants a ticket for the Star map show. What can she do at 2:00 PM?
options: See the Star map show. She is in time for a ticket.
See the Moon show in the Dome Theater.
Go to the meteorite touch table. It needs no ticket.
Wait for the next Star map show at 3:00 PM.
items.hint: Read the note about tickets. Work out the last time to get a Star map ticket. Then look across the 2:00 PM row for something else to do.
items.explain: She can go to the meteorite touch table. The desk stops giving tickets 15 minutes before a show, so the last time for a 2:00 PM ticket is 1:45 PM. The 2:00 PM row shows the meteorite touch table, and the note says other rooms need no ticket.

items.prompt: Sam wants to build a paper rocket, see the Star map show and visit the meteorite touch table. He will also eat lunch. Put his day in order so nothing happens at the same time.
items.hint: Start with the event that happens at only one time. Then fit the other events into the times that are left.
items.explain: Paper rocket at 10:00 AM, lunch at 12:00 PM, the meteorite table at 1:00 PM, then the Star map show at 2:00 PM. The Star map show is only at 2:00 PM, so the rocket and the meteorite table must go at other times.

items.prompt: Ben wants to watch the giraffes eat. What time should he be at Tall Tree Yard?
items.hint: Find the row that says Giraffes. Then look across to the Time column.
items.explain: He should be there at 11:00 AM. It is in the Giraffes row.

items.prompt: It is 1:30 PM. Sam wants to see an animal eat. Tap the place he should go.
items.hint: Find 1:30 PM in the Time column. Then read across to the Place column.
items.explain: Sam goes to the Kelp Pool. The 1:30 PM row says Sea otters at the Kelp Pool.

items.prompt: Maya's dad wants an easy trail that takes 1 hour. Which trail should they pick?
items.hint: Look down the Level column for the easy trails. Then check the Time column for each of them.
items.explain: They should pick the Fern Path. It is Easy and takes 1 hour. The Creek Loop and the Old Mill Walk are easy too, but they are shorter.

items.prompt: It rained hard last night. Sam wants to see the view of Lantern Peaks. What should he do?
options: Hike the Ridge Trail this morning.
Hike the Creek Loop to see the view.
Hike a different trail today, and save the Ridge Trail for a dry day.
Hike the Ridge Trail with Pixel on a leash.
items.hint: Find the trail with the view. Then read the note under the table for a rule about rain.
items.explain: He should hike a different trail today and save the Ridge Trail for a dry day. The Ridge Trail has the view of Lantern Peaks, but the note says it is closed after heavy rain.

items.prompt: Maya's dad has 1 hour for a hike. Sort the trails by how long they take.
items.hint: Read the Time column for each trail. Compare each time with 1 hour.
items.explain: The Old Mill Walk (20 minutes), Creek Loop (30 minutes) and Fern Path (1 hour) take 1 hour or less. The Mill Pond Trail (1 hour 30 minutes) and Ridge Trail (3 hours) take more. Look in the Time column.

items.prompt: Leo plays in the Drum Club. What time does his group start to play?
items.hint: Find the group that plays before the Drum Club. Add its length to the start time.
items.explain: The Drum Club starts at 6:05 PM. The music night starts at 6:00 PM, and the Grade 6 Choir plays first for 5 minutes.

items.prompt: Sam's family gets to the music night at 6:20 PM. Tap the row for the group that is playing when they arrive.
items.hint: Start at 6:00 PM. Add each length in order until you pass 6:20 PM.
items.explain: Tap the Grade 7 Band row. The choir plays from 6:00 to 6:05 PM, the Drum Club from 6:05 to 6:15 PM, and the Grade 7 Band from 6:15 to 6:25 PM.

items.prompt: Ben's mom will pick him up when the music night ends. What time does it end?
items.hint: Add up every number in the Length column, the break too. Then add the total to the start time.
items.explain: The music night ends at 6:55 PM. The lengths add up to 5 + 10 + 10 + 15 + 5 + 10 = 55 minutes, and 55 minutes after 6:00 PM is 6:55 PM.

items.prompt: Grandma Rose has a ticket for the 11:00 AM ferry on Sunday. What will happen to her trip?
options: It is canceled. She can use her ticket on the 12:30 PM Osprey.
It sails at 11:00 AM, because the wind is under 30 mph.
It is canceled. She can use her ticket on the 2:00 PM Puffin.
It is canceled. She must buy a new ticket for a later trip.
items.hint: Find which boat her trip uses and its wind forecast. Check the note for that boat's limit. Then look for the next trip that can sail.
items.explain: Her trip is canceled, and she can use her ticket on the 12:30 PM Osprey. The 11:00 AM trip is on the Puffin, and the note says the Puffin stays in the harbor at 25 mph or more. The next trip, the 12:30 PM Osprey, sails because 35 mph is under its 40 mph limit.

items.prompt: Ana must be on Gull Island by 1:00 PM on Sunday. What is the latest ferry she can take from Harbor Town?
items.hint: Add 40 minutes to each time to see when it gets to Gull Island. Then use the note to check if the boat can sail in that wind.
items.explain: She should take the 9:30 AM ferry. The 12:30 PM ferry gets in at 1:10 PM, which is too late. The 11:00 AM Puffin is canceled because the wind is 25 mph. The 9:30 AM Puffin sails in 15 mph wind and gets in at 10:10 AM.

items.prompt: Sort each Sunday trip. Will it sail?
items.hint: Check which boat each trip uses. Then compare its wind forecast with that boat's limit in the note.
items.explain: The 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM Puffin trips are canceled, because their wind is 25 mph or more. All the other trips sail. The Osprey sails in winds up to 40 mph, so even the 12:30 PM trip in 35 mph wind sails.

items.prompt: Grandma Rose books the Deep Level Tour for herself, Sam and Leo. Sam is 12 and Leo is 13. How much will she pay?
items.hint: Use the note to find the price for each person's age. Then add the three prices.
items.explain: She pays $22. Sam and Leo are ages 6 to 17, so each pays $6. Grandma Rose is an adult and pays $10. $6 + $6 + $10 = $22.

items.prompt: Ana, Ben and their cousin, who is 7, get to the mine at 9:45 AM. They want to take a tour together. Which is the first tour all three can go on?
items.hint: Check the Starts time against 9:45 AM. Then check the Ages column for a 7-year-old, and the Spots left column for 3 people.
items.explain: The first tour they can all go on is the Mine Train Ride at 1:00 PM. The 9:30 AM walk has already started, the 10:00 AM train has 0 spots left, and the Deep Level Tour is for ages 10 and up, so their cousin is too young.

items.prompt: Maya and her mom get to the mine at 12:00 PM. They must leave by 2:15 PM. Tap the row for the tour they can take from start to end.
items.hint: Look only at tours that start after 12:00 PM. Add each tour's length to its start time, and compare the end time with 2:15 PM.
items.explain: Tap the 1:00 PM Mine Train Ride row. It runs from 1:00 to 2:00 PM and has 5 spots left. The 1:30 PM Deep Level Tour ends at 3:30 PM, and the 3:00 PM walk starts after they leave.

items.prompt: Maya is 11 and Leo is 13. They get to the Nature Center at 1:45 PM on Saturday. Which program can they both join from the start?
items.hint: Find the programs that start after 1:45 PM. Then check the Ages column for both of them.
items.explain: They can both join Tree Detectives at 2:00 PM. It is for ages 8 and up. The Owl Talk ends at 1:30 PM, and the Night Sounds Walk is for ages 12 and up, so Maya is too young.

items.prompt: Sam is 12. He is at the Bird Walk at 8:00 AM. He also wants a place on the Night Sounds Walk. What should he do?
options: Go to the campsite gate at 7:30 PM. That walk has no sign-up.
Sign up at the campsite gate at 7:30 PM.
Bring an adult, because he is under 12.
Sign up at the front desk at 9:00 AM, after the Bird Walk.
items.hint: Find the Sign-up? column for the Night Sounds Walk. Then read the note to see where and when sign-up happens.
items.explain: He should sign up at the front desk at 9:00 AM. The Night Sounds Walk row says Yes for sign-up, and the note says sign-up opens at 9:00 AM at the front desk and places fill up fast. The Bird Walk ends at 9:00 AM, so he can go straight there.

items.prompt: Leo watches all of the Static Comets set. Then he walks to the Harbor Tent to see The Fog Horns. How many minutes of The Fog Horns' set will he hear?
items.hint: Work out when the Static Comets set ends, and add the walk. Then work out when The Fog Horns' set ends.
items.explain: He hears 20 minutes. Static Comets play from 2:00 to 2:45 PM. After the 10-minute walk, Leo gets to the tent at 2:55 PM. The Fog Horns play from 2:30 to 3:15 PM, and 2:55 to 3:15 PM is 20 minutes.

items.prompt: Leo brings his own drum. He wants to play in the whole Drum Circle and then see all of The Lanterns. Can he do both?
options: Yes. The Drum Circle ends at 12:45 PM, so he has time to walk.
Yes. The Drum Circle ends at 1:15 PM, and The Lanterns start at 1:30 PM.
No. The Drum Circle ends at 1:15 PM, but The Lanterns start at 1:00 PM.
No. The Drum Circle is for ages 12 and up.
items.hint: Use the note to work out when the Drum Circle ends. Then compare that with the time The Lanterns start.
items.explain: No, he cannot do both. Every set lasts 45 minutes, so the Drum Circle runs from 12:30 to 1:15 PM. The Lanterns start at 1:00 PM on the Main Stage, before the Drum Circle ends.

items.prompt: Maya is 11. She has no instrument with her. She wants to learn to play one at the festival. Tap the row for the workshop she can join.
items.hint: Find every act where people play. Check the About the act column for the age rule and for who brings the instrument.
items.explain: Tap the Ukulele for Beginners row. It is for ages 8 and up, and ukuleles are lent. The Steel Drum Workshop is for ages 12 and up, and at the Drum Circle you bring your own drum.

items.prompt: Ms. Ortiz is a museum member. Sam is 12 and Maya is 11, and they pay for entry. Both of them also do the 2:00 PM Fossil Lab. How much do the three of them pay in all?
items.hint: Use the note to find the entry price for each person. Then add the Fossil Lab price for each person who does it.
items.explain: They pay $22. Ms. Ortiz is a member, so she gets in free. Sam and Maya pay $7 each for entry, and $4 each for the Fossil Lab. $7 + $7 + $4 + $4 = $22.

items.prompt: It is 10:20 AM. The front desk says the 10:30 AM Fossil Lab is full. Maya still wants to clean a fossil and see the film. What is her best plan?
options: See the film at 11:00 AM, then do the Fossil Lab at 2:00 PM.
Do the Fossil Lab at 10:30 AM, then see the film.
See the film at 11:00 AM, then clean a fossil at the Dig Pit.
Do the Fossil Lab at 2:00 PM, then see the film at 3:00 PM.
items.hint: Find every row for the Fossil Lab and every row for the film. Cross out the full lab. Then check that the times you pick are in the table.
items.explain: Her best plan is the film at 11:00 AM and the Fossil Lab at 2:00 PM. The 10:30 AM lab is full, and the film is shown only at 11:00 AM. The Dig Pit is for model bones, and 3:00 PM is a talk, not the film.

items.prompt: Sam is at the Dig Pit. He must leave the museum at 3:15 PM to catch his bus. Tap the row for the one event he can do from start to end after the Dig Pit.
items.hint: Find when the Dig Pit ends. Look for an event that starts after that and ends before 3:15 PM.
items.explain: Tap the 2:00 PM Fossil Lab row. The Dig Pit ends at 1:45 PM, and the lab runs from 2:00 to 3:00 PM. The 1:00 PM tour starts during the Dig Pit, and the 3:00 PM talk ends at 3:30 PM, after Sam leaves.

items.prompt: Which rock does Maya still need to find?
items.hint: Look for the rock with no check mark next to it.
items.explain: Maya still needs to find garnet. Garnet is the only rock on the list with no check mark.

items.prompt: How many rocks has Maya found?
items.hint: Count only the rocks with a check mark.
items.explain: Maya found three rocks: quartz, mica and pyrite. Each one has a check mark.

items.prompt: Ben loves soccer. What time is the soccer robot show?
items.hint: Find the row that says Soccer robot. Then look across to the time.
items.explain: The soccer robot show is at 1 PM. It is in the Soccer robot row.

items.prompt: It is 11 AM. Tap the robot that has a show now.
items.hint: Find 11 AM in the Show time column. Then look across to the robot.
items.explain: The drawing robot has a show at 11 AM. It is in the Drawing robot row.

items.prompt: Sam wants raisin bread. What day should he go to the bakery?
items.hint: Find the row with raisin bread. Then read the day in the same row.
items.explain: He should go on Friday. The Friday row says Raisin bread.

items.prompt: Sam goes to the bakery on Tuesday. Is there a bread of the day?
options: No. Tuesday is not on the sign.
items.hint: Read the Day column from top to bottom. Look for Tuesday.
items.explain: No. The sign has a row for Monday and a row for Wednesday, but no row for Tuesday.

items.prompt: The twins want free swim in the afternoon. What time does it start?
items.hint: Find the rows that say Free swim. Pick the one with a PM time.
items.explain: Afternoon free swim starts at 3:00 PM. It is in the last row. At 1:00 PM there is lap swim for ages 16 and up.

items.prompt: Ben gets to the pool at 12:30 PM. Tap the row that shows what is on then.
items.hint: Find the row that starts before 12:30 PM and ends after it.
items.explain: Tap the 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM row. The pool is closed for cleaning then.

items.prompt: Ana is 12. Can she go to lap swim?
options: Yes. It is for all ages.
No. It is for ages 16 and up.
Yes, but only in the morning.
items.hint: Find the row for lap swim. Read the ages in that row.
items.explain: No. The lap swim row says ages 16 and up, and Ana is 12.

items.prompt: Grandma Rose must be back by 12:00 PM. Which trip should they take?
items.hint: Look down the Comes back column. Find a time before 12:00 PM.
items.explain: They should take the 9:00 AM Blue Fin trip. It comes back at 11:00 AM. The Sea Star trip comes back at 1:00 PM, which is too late.

items.prompt: What time does the last trip of the day come back?
items.hint: Find the last row. Then look across to the Comes back column.
items.explain: The last trip comes back at 5:30 PM. It is the 3:00 PM Sea Star trip in the last row.

items.prompt: Leo wants to skate on a sunny day. Which day should he go?
items.hint: Look down the Weather column for the word sunny.
items.explain: He should go on Saturday. The Saturday row says Sunny.

items.prompt: On which day does Leo need a raincoat if he goes out?
items.hint: Read the Weather column. Find the day with rain.
items.explain: He needs a raincoat on Friday. The Friday row says Rain all day.

items.prompt: Tap the row for the coldest day.
items.hint: Look down the High column. Find the smallest number.
items.explain: Tap the Sunday row. Its high is 54°F, the lowest of the three days.

items.prompt: Which game takes the most tokens?
items.hint: Look down the Tokens column. Find the biggest number.
items.explain: Dance Floor takes the most. It takes 4 tokens for one play.

items.prompt: Ana has 4 tokens. She plays Space Racer one time. How many tokens does she have left?
items.hint: Find how many tokens Space Racer takes. Take that number away from 4.
items.explain: She has 2 tokens left. Space Racer takes 2 tokens, and 4 - 2 = 2.

items.prompt: Ben has 2 tokens. Sort the games.
items.hint: Read the tokens for each game. Check if it is 2 or less.
items.explain: Ben can play Space Racer, Air hockey and the Claw machine, because they take 2 tokens or less. Robot Maze takes 3 and Dance Floor takes 4.

items.prompt: Maya plays the flute. What day is her lesson?
items.hint: Find the row for Flute. Then look across to the Day column.
items.explain: Her lesson is on Monday. The Flute row says Monday at 4:45 PM.

items.prompt: Sam plays guitar. Priya plays cello. On which day do they both have a lesson?
items.hint: Find the Guitar row and the Cello row. Compare their days.
items.explain: They both have a lesson on Monday. The Guitar row and the Cello row both say Monday.

items.prompt: Sam wants to see dinosaur eggs. Which floor should he go to?
items.hint: Read each row. Look for the words dinosaur eggs.
items.explain: He should go to Floor 4. The Floor 4 row says Dinosaur eggs and nests.

items.prompt: Maya wants to see the big skeletons. Tap the elevator button she should press.
items.hint: Find the row that tells about big skeletons. Read its floor number.
items.explain: She presses 2. The Floor 2 row says Dinosaur Hall: big dinosaur skeletons.

items.prompt: Sam gets to Harbor Town Station at 7:30 AM. He wants to get to Pine Bay as early as he can. Which train should he take?
items.hint: Find the trains that leave Harbor Town Station after 7:30 AM. Then compare when they get to Pine Bay.
items.explain: He should take Train 2, the Express. Train 1 left at 7:10 AM. Train 2 leaves at 8:00 AM and gets to Pine Bay at 8:35 AM, before Train 3.

items.prompt: Maya wants to get off at Sandy Cove. Which trains stop there?
items.hint: Find the Sandy Cove row. Read the note to learn what a dash means.
items.explain: Train 1 and Train 3 stop at Sandy Cove. The Sandy Cove row has a dash for Train 2, and the note says a dash means the train does not stop there.

items.prompt: How long does Train 3 take to go from Harbor Town Station to Pine Bay?
items.hint: Find the Train 3 time at Harbor Town Station and at Pine Bay. Count the minutes from the first time to the second.
items.explain: Train 3 takes 55 minutes. It leaves Harbor Town Station at 9:15 AM and gets to Pine Bay at 10:10 AM.

items.prompt: Priya buys veggie noodles and a fruit ice pop. How much of her $8 is left?
items.hint: Add the prices of the two things she buys. Then take the total away from $8.
items.explain: She has $0 left. Veggie noodles cost $6 and a fruit ice pop costs $2. $6 + $2 = $8, and $8 - $8 = $0.

items.prompt: Maya buys two bean tacos and corn on a stick. Then she wants a sweet treat. What can she buy with the money she has left?
items.hint: Add up what she buys first and take it away from $8. Then compare what is left with the prices at Scoop Shack.
items.explain: She cannot buy a sweet treat. Tacos cost $5 and corn costs $2, so she spends $7 and has $1 left. The cheapest treat, the fruit ice pop, costs $2.

items.prompt: Leo wants the cheapest food at Noodle Boat. Tap its row.
items.hint: Find the two Noodle Boat rows. Compare their prices.
items.explain: Tap the Egg roll row. At Noodle Boat, an egg roll costs $2 and veggie noodles cost $6.

items.prompt: What time must Ana and Ben arrive on Saturday?
items.hint: Find the Hawks' first game. Then read the note about when to arrive.
items.explain: They must arrive at 8:30 AM. The Hawks' first game is at 9:00 AM, and the note says to arrive 30 minutes before the first game.

items.prompt: What time does the Hawks' last game end?
items.hint: Find the Hawks' latest game. Add the game length from the note to its start time.
items.explain: It ends at 12:50 PM. The last Hawks game starts at 12:00 PM, and the note says each game lasts 50 minutes.

items.prompt: Sort the games. Which ones do the Hawks play in?
items.hint: Read each row. Look for Harbor Hawks in the Team column, then read the time and the field.
items.explain: The Hawks play at 9:00 AM on Field 1, at 10:30 AM on Field 2 and at 12:00 PM on Field 1. The other three games are for other teams.

items.prompt: Sam wants to see craters on the Moon. Which date should he go?
items.hint: Find the Moon in the What to look at column. Then read the date in that row.
items.explain: He should go on Friday, May 22. That row says Craters on the Moon.

items.prompt: On Saturday, May 16, the sky is full of clouds. What happens to the sky night?
options: Visitors look at the Moon instead.
items.hint: Read the note under the table. Find what happens when the sky is cloudy.
items.explain: It is canceled. The note says sky nights are canceled if the sky is cloudy.

items.prompt: Priya wants to look at a planet through the telescope. Which date should she pick?
items.hint: Read each row in the What to look at column. Think about which one is a planet.
items.explain: She should pick Friday, May 8. Jupiter is a planet. Star clusters and double stars are stars, and the Moon is not a planet.

items.prompt: Maya wants to find pyrite. On which date should she go?
items.hint: Look down the Look for column for pyrite. Then read the date in that row.
items.explain: She should go on Saturday, April 18. The Ridgeway Mine Museum row says Copper ore and pyrite.

items.prompt: Maya packs a warm jacket. Which trip is she packing for, and where does she meet the club?
options: The beach trip. She meets at the library.
The creek trip. She meets at the creek.
The mine trip. She meets at the library.
The mine trip. She meets at the mine.
items.hint: Find the row with a jacket in the Bring column. Then read the note to see where to meet.
items.explain: She is packing for the Ridgeway Mine Museum trip on April 18. The note says to meet at the library at 9:00 AM on every trip day.

items.prompt: Leo can come only in May. Tap the row for the trip he can join.
items.hint: Read the Date column. Find the month of May.
items.explain: Tap the Gull Point beach row. It is the only trip in May, on Saturday, May 2.

items.prompt: Which robot was the fastest in Heat 1?
items.hint: Look at the three Heat 1 rows. Find the smallest time.
items.explain: Spark was the fastest in Heat 1. It finished in 36 seconds, the smallest time in that heat.

items.prompt: Sort the robots. Which ones race in the final?
items.hint: Read the note. Then find the two smallest times in each heat.
items.explain: Spark and Zip go on from Heat 1. Priya's rover and Bolt go on from Heat 2. Gizmo and Pebble had the biggest time in their heats, so they are out.

items.prompt: How many seconds faster was Priya's rover than Bolt?
items.hint: Find both times. Take the smaller time away from the bigger time.
items.explain: Priya's rover was 4 seconds faster. Bolt took 39 seconds and her rover took 35 seconds. 39 - 35 = 4.

items.prompt: At what time is rain most likely?
items.hint: Look down the Chance of rain column. Find the biggest number.
items.explain: Rain is most likely at 9 AM. The chance of rain is 90%, the biggest number in that column.

items.prompt: What is the best time to fly the kite?
items.hint: Read the note. Find a time with wind from 8 to 20 mph. Then check that the chance of rain is low.
items.explain: 3 PM is best. The wind is 14 mph, which is inside the 8 to 20 mph range, and the chance of rain is only 10%. At 9 AM there is wind, but it will probably rain.

items.prompt: Sam wants to walk Pixel when there is no chance of rain at all. Tap that row.
items.hint: Look down the Chance of rain column for 0%.
items.explain: Tap the 5 PM row. The chance of rain is 0%.

items.prompt: Maya can go to the beach only on Saturday afternoon. What time is low tide then?
items.hint: Find the Saturday row and the Low tides column. Pick the time that is in the afternoon.
items.explain: Low tide is at 4:55 PM. The Saturday row has two low tides, and 4:55 PM is the PM one. 4:05 PM is on Friday.

items.prompt: On Sunday, what time is the first high tide?
items.hint: Find the Sunday row. Then look in the High tides column for the earlier time.
items.explain: The first high tide on Sunday is at 11:30 AM. It is the first time in the High tides column of the Sunday row.

items.prompt: Look at the morning low tide on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. What happens to its time each day?
options: It comes about 50 minutes later each day.
It comes at the same time each day.
It comes about 50 minutes earlier each day.
It comes about 2 hours later each day.
items.hint: Read the AM low tide for each day. Count the minutes from one day to the next.

items.prompt: The team needs 28 slices. Which order has enough slices for the lowest price?

items.prompt: Maya, who is 11, and her mom want to see the seals on Saturday. What time does their tour leave?

items.prompt: The club rides from Harbor Town to Gull Point, then to Sandy Cove, then straight back to Harbor Town. How many miles is the whole ride?
items.hint: Find the miles for each part of the ride, one pair of places at a time. Then add the three numbers.
items.explain: The whole ride is 25 miles. Harbor Town to Gull Point is 6 miles, Gull Point to Sandy Cove is 7 miles, and Sandy Cove back to Harbor Town is 12 miles. 6 + 7 + 12 = 25.

items.prompt: The club leaves Harbor Town at 9:00 AM and rides straight to Pine Bay. About what time will they get there?

items.explain: They get there at about 11:00 AM. Harbor Town to Pine Bay is 20 miles. The note says riders go about 10 miles in 1 hour, so 20 miles takes about 2 hours.

items.prompt: Mr. Okafor wants a ride from Harbor Town to one place and back on the same road. The whole ride must be at least 20 miles and no more than 30 miles. Where should they ride to?
items.hint: Find the miles from Harbor Town to each place. Double each number for there and back, then compare with 20 and 30.
items.explain: They should ride to Sandy Cove. It is 12 miles each way, so the whole ride is 24 miles. Gull Point (12 miles in all) and Lantern Peaks (16 miles in all) are too short, and Pine Bay (40 miles in all) is too long.

steps.say: I need the time the park opens on Saturday.
I look down the Days column for Saturday. It is in the second row.
I look across that row to the Open column. It says 9 AM to 5 PM.
The first time is when the park opens. The second time is when it closes.
So the park opens at 9 AM on Saturday.
